Indeed, each incircle is tangent to the shared edge, and if both touch it at the same point $P$, then both circles pass through $P$ with tangent direction along the edge, so they are tangent to each other at $P$.

**Tangent point formula.** In triangle $ABC$ with $a = BC$, $b = CA$, $c = AB$, and $s = (a+b+c)/2$, the incircle touches side $AB$ at distance $s - a = (b + c - a)/2$ from $A$.

**Computing the six conditions.** For each edge, equate the two tangent-point distances from the shared vertex:

| Edge | Faces | Condition for tangency |
|------|-------|----------------------|

| $AC$ | $ABC, ACD$ | $\frac{AB+AC-BC}{2} = \frac{AC+AD-CD}{2}$, i.e. $AB + CD = AD + BC$ |
| $AD$ | $ABD, ACD$ | $\frac{AB+AD-BD}{2} = \frac{AC+AD-CD}{2}$, i.e. $AB + CD = AC + BD$ |
| $BC$ | $ABC, BCD$ | $\frac{AB+BC-AC}{2} = \frac{BC+BD-CD}{2}$, i.e. $AB + CD = AC + BD$ |
| $BD$ | $ABD, BCD$ | $\frac{AB+BD-AD}{2} = \frac{BC+BD-CD}{2}$, i.e. $AB + CD = AD + BC$ |
| $CD$ | $ACD, BCD$ | $\frac{AC+CD-AD}{2} = \frac{BC+CD-BD}{2}$, i.e. $AC + BD = AD + BC$ |

These yield three distinct equations:

Since (III) follows from (I) and (II), condition (a) — all six pairs tangent — is equivalent to (I) $\wedge$ (II), which is equivalent to
$$AB + CD = AC + BD = AD + BC,$$
